scope: Read exact 131-patch CI manifest, replay onto original pinned XNU selected files, inspect resulting definitions/functions. No compilation or kernel edit.

items.name: 47-bit user TTBR0 and four-level user pmap
items.existing: macos-user-address-space.patch changes MACH_VM_MAX_ADDRESS_RAW and commpage assertion only; T0SZ_BOOT remains 26 for 4K/subpage L1, with no T0SZ_USER override.
required: T0SZ_USER=17 and TCR_EL1_KVA_ENTRY/EPD0 policy in proc_reg.h
pmap_pt_attr_4k_user, native_user_pt_attr, root allocation assertion and kernel/user geometry selection
arm_init early TCR update before signing, arm_vm_init handoff and secondary arm_init_tramp TCR update
pmap_user_va_bits, sleh PAC fault mask and VM_USER_STRIP_MASK use the user range

items.name: wimg_to_pte managed DRAM outside low classification range
items.existing: VM_WIMG_RT and VM_WIMG_WCOMB branches check is_dram_addr(pa) only.
required: In these two branches, recognize is_dram_addr(pa) || pa_valid(pa). pa_valid establishes managed ownership; do not label every high address DRAM.

items.name: CACHE_ATTRINDX_RT native non-Apple normal-memory selection
items.existing: The WRITECOMB define already exists under HAS_UCNORMAL_MEM || APPLEVIRTUALPLATFORM; native BCM2837 does not select it and instead gets POSTED_COMBINED_REORDERED.
required: Add native target to the Normal noncacheable WRITECOMB selection, scoped to actual native build; preserve Device mappings for MMIO.

items.name: pmap_batch_set_cache_attributes_internal non-RT cache synchronization
items.existing: Original batch state machine has a dedicated RT cache-flush pass. It lacks the extra pmap_sync_wimg call on changed non-RT attributes; pmap_set_cache_attributes has its own synchronization.
required: After pvh_unlock in update pass, for wimg_bits_new != wimg_bits_prev && wimg_bits_new != VM_WIMG_RT call pmap_sync_wimg(pn,wimg_bits_prev,wimg_bits_new); preserve existing RT pass.

numeric_correction: 0x7FFFFE000000 is 128 TiB minus 32 MiB, not 512 GiB. 455-512 GiB is the user mapping region discussed by the patch; it exceeds the current 38-bit (256 GiB) TTBR0 range.
